whatItDoes: Shows how many months of expenses your current savings cover and how far you are from a target emergency fund (commonly 3-6 months of expenses).
whyItExists: Emergency savings is the shock absorber between you and debt. Knowing your coverage in months makes the goal concrete and the gap clear, so you can plan how much to save.
whoShouldUse: Anyone building an emergency fund, budgeting households, and people recovering a depleted buffer after an expense.
useCases: See how many months current savings cover
Find the target amount for your goal months
Track progress as the fund grows
Plan a monthly savings goal if you're short
instructions: Enter your current emergency fund balance
Read the months covered and target amount
examples: $4,000/month expenses and $20,000 saved -> about 5 months covered
bestPractices: Use a realistic average of essential monthly expenses
Keep the fund accessible, in a liquid low-risk account
Choose 3-6 months based on income stability
Rebuild the fund after using it via a regular contribution
commonMistakes: Using net-of-discretionary expenses that drift with lifestyle
Keeping the fund in illiquid or volatile investments
Setting a target that doesn't match income stability
faq: What is a good emergency fund? — Usually 3-6 months of essential expenses.
Should I also plan other savings? — This covers emergencies only; other goals need separate planning.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
